Theme

Body, health & movement · School & learning

gene noun

also genes, genetic, genetics, DNA, in the genes, inherited

modern

M-O s.v. gene (Egger, S.L. 80)

1Classical Latin speaks of inheritance through the parents and nature: what a child takes from them is ā parentibus acceptum or ā patre, and a family likeness lies in the stirps or genus. These say “it runs in the family”, not “gene”.

nota genetica1

a gene

Egger’s phrase, a “mark of descent”, the first that Morgan–Owens gives. The adjective geneticus, genetica, geneticum (genetic) is modern too, made on Greek γενετικός; genetics is genetica or doctrīna genetica (M-O s.v. genetics).

Other words

  • genum, genī n. — a gene

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. gene (Helfer; Lexicon recentis Latinitatis) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A short coinage on the modern languages’ word; Morgan–Owens marks it as less recommended than Egger’s phrase.

See also body, science, health.

SourcesMorgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.vv. gene, genetic, genetics.

No classical source, nor Traupman nor Levi & Bini, has a word for a gene.
